findings.title: Write lock held across manifest load and can clear a filled cache
findings.body: GetWebAssets copies entryPointAssetsCache under a read lock, drops that lock, then at line 48 takes the exclusive lock and holds it for the whole readWebAssetsFromFile call (line 60). It never re-reads the cache after acquiring the write lock, and line 69 always stores result, including nil. Callers that all observed a nil cache therefore each load the manifest while holding the process-wide mutex, so a startup burst does N sequential disk reads and blocks every other GetWebAssets for that I/O. In Dev the fast path is skipped on purpose, so every call takes this exclusive section and asset loads are globally serialized on disk I/O. A waiter whose load fails after another caller already published a value replaces that cache with nil, so later non-dev requests miss and reload. Load outside the lock; under the lock, return the existing cache when not in Dev and it is already set, and do not store a nil result over a populated cache.

findings.title: No concurrent test for the cache race fix
findings.body: This change only wraps the global entryPointAssetsCache in a mutex inside GetWebAssets and adds no test. Nothing runs concurrent GetWebAssets calls under the race detector, or checks that a successful fill is reused by waiters and is not cleared by a concurrent failed load. The data race this PR is fixing can come back with no regression coverage.
